.SHORT TERM /THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Issued at 245 AM CDT Wed Jul 22 2026

Temperatures are already dropping into the 60s and 70s early this 
morning as northerly winds advect cooler and less humid air into the 
area early this morning.  The low level flow will continue through 
tonight as the HREF is showing a surface high moving from the Upper 
Midwest into the Great Lakes.  Mainly dry weather is expected the 
through Thursday with the dry low level flow underneath northwest 
flow aloft.  With only fair weather cumulus today and tomorrow, 
highs will only range from the upper 70s over parts of eastern CWA 
to mid 80s over central and southeast Missouri.

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY NIGHT THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Issued at 245 AM CDT Wed Jul 22 2026

The GFS/ECMWF is showing an upper ridge building over the western 
CONUS Thursday into Friday which keeps northwest upper flow over 
Missouri and Illinois.  Showers and thunderstorm chances will 
increase over the area beginning late Thursday night and continues 
into Saturday with the NBM/LREF showing the highest chances (40-70%) 
on Friday morning when the low level jet will be focused over the 
area. There will also be a upper trough that will move across 
Missouri and Illinois that both the determistic models and the LREF 
is showing timing differences which keeps PoPs in the forecast into 
Saturday.   This spread in timing will decrease in coming days as 
the models come into the better agreement.  The LREF is showing 
PWATS around 2" and WPC is highlighting most of the Missouri 
counties in slight risk for excessive rainfall on Friday. The LREF 
then shows the upper ridge shifting east and building over the 
central CONUS.  This keeps the area mainly dry from late weekend 
through the first part of next week.

Temperatures on Friday will remain cool with clouds, the chance of 
rain, and the cool surface flow.  Highs will begin to warm back 
above normal by Sunday as a warm front moves back through the area 
and 850mb temperatures climb back above 20C.
